notes.1a: Most candidates correctly calculated the net book value of the freehold property but relatively few were able to calculate the cost and accumulated depreciation of the plant and machinery and motor vehicles.
notes.1b: Many candidates did not answer this question well. Very few candidates made any adjustment to the retained earnings and some adjusted the trade receivables incorrectly.
notes.1c: Some candidates did not answer the question by providing descriptions of the different methods of depreciation. Those that did address the requirements of the question generally gave two or three appropriate factors.
notes.1d: Many candidates gave the required advice and three relevant comments. Few, however, supported their answer with ratios. Those who did calculate the current gearing ratio and the gearing ratio after raising the finance were able to score full marks for the question.
notes.2i: Most candidates identified that the profit on consignment would be overstated as the expenses were understated. However, the amount of the profit overstatement was not calculated correctly.
notes.2ii: Very few candidates calculated the amount by which the profit for the year was understated.
notes.2b: The consignment account was well prepared with most candidates being awarded at least six of the ten available marks. A limited number produced a fully correct account and were awarded ten marks. The most common errors were the incorrect calculation of the closing balance and incorrect labelling of the income statement and/or the closing balance.
notes.2c: Performance was mixed with some correct calculations but also many omitting the balance of $32500 and/or the balance from the consignment account.
notes.2d: Most candidates identified the probable saving on transport costs and the wider market but few provided any other valid points.
